response.consequence: Redundant file I/O and JSON parsing, serialized under the lock, on a cold start. The result is correct, so the impact is small.
response.explanation: The change reads the cache under RLock, releases it, then takes the write Lock. It never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. When the cache is empty at startup, N concurrent requests all pass the nil check. They then queue on the mutex, and each one in turn re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json and overwrites the cache. The same happens after a failed load, because the failure leaves the cache nil. There is no API or wire contract break. The exported signature and return types are unchanged.
response.title: No cache re-check after taking the write lock, so every queued caller re-reads the manifest
